raw_response:
I'm 48, been working these 9.2 mu for 20 years now. Never went to school, but I know my land and I know what works. My old man farmed this land before me, and now it's just me and my wife — two mouths to feed, two pairs of hands to do the work. We don't have much cash, so every yuan I spend on inputs has to count. I can't afford to waste money on things that might not work.

This year I'll do what I always do: cabbage first, then chinesecabbage after harvest, then spinach in winter. That's my rotation. The chili, eggplant, and kidney bean are on the small plot near the house — mostly for our own eating, though if there's extra I'll sell some at the county market.

For the cabbage, I plant around mid-March when the soil warms up a bit. Last year I got about 3000 jin per mu, so this year I'm hoping for the same if the weather holds. I buy my seeds from the shop in town — not those fancy hybrids, just the regular kind that grows steady. Costs me about 40 yuan per mu. I put down one big bag of compound fertilizer and half a bag of urea per mu, same as always. Lao Wang down the road does the same and his cabbage looks fine. I irrigate maybe three times from the well — pumping costs electricity, so I don't water unless it's really dry. If I see cabbage worms, I spray once, maybe twice. For transplanting and harvest, my wife and I can't do it all alone on 3 mu, so I hire two people for a couple days each. That costs money, but we have to.

After cabbage comes off in mid-June, I quickly till the land and plant chinesecabbage in mid-July. The turnaround isn't as tight as wheat-maize, but I still can't dawdle. Chinesecabbage needs about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. I don't put as much as cabbage — it seems to grow fine with less. Maybe 2-3 times irrigation if July and August are hot and dry. I hire help again for transplanting, maybe two days. Last year I got about 4000 jin per mu, hoping for that again.

Spinach goes in early November after chinesecabbage is out. I plant about 2 mu. Spinach doesn't need much — half a bag of compound fertilizer and some manure I saved. Maybe irrigate once if winter is dry. My wife and I can handle the work ourselves. Should get about 2000 jin per mu by February or March.

The small plot near the house — half mu of chili, half mu of eggplant, and a bit of kidney bean. These are for us to eat. I don't spend much money on them. Some compound fertilizer, a little manure. If bugs come, I spray. If not, I don't bother. The eggplant I buy seedlings from the market because starting from seed is too much trouble. The kidney bean I just keep some seeds from last year.

Total cost this year? I figure about 3000 yuan for everything — seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, hired labor, and electricity for the pump. That's a lot for us, but we need to spend it to eat.
